positive_changes: aftercare.py:173-178,200-225: numeric sorting fixes lexical AC-1000 placement without changing canonical serialization or schema. For accepted states the unchanged positional equality requires exactly AC-001 through AC-N and matching record IDs. Unicode digits, leading-zero aliases, foreign keys, missing IDs and two different keys with the same numeric value cannot pass that equality. Accepted reconstruction has unique numeric sort keys and is deterministic regardless of insertion order.

Validation still precedes request replay inside _parse/_validate, and authorization/input validation in record_concern is untouched. Malformed states remain rejected. Sorting can change which malformed entry is reported first; an extremely long digit suffix can raise ValueError in int conversion earlier, still mapped to StateInvalid by _validate. No newly accepted malformed state or write-after-invalid-state path identified.

test_aftercare.py:307-340 exercises text-sorted and reversed 999/1000/1001 snapshots and subsequent ID allocation, plus gap, noncanonical alias, foreign key and mismatched record ID rejection. Tests are behavioral, not constant-only assertions.

test_aftercare_store.py:193-234 seeds synthetic valid receipts/request mappings, performs real 1000/1001 writes, reopens each adapter, verifies numeric restore and same-request replay. Seed cloning avoids 1000 expensive writes but boundary writes are genuine. Existing replay-no-write and conflict tests remain in the shared adapter contract.
